subject: FinWise privacy follow-up — DPA intake & SCC routing (post-demo)
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Koval <elena.koval@finwise.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, david_kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FinWise privacy follow-up — DPA intake & SCC routing (post-demo)

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to meet you and the FinWise team. Quick recap from our side and three asks to keep things moving from a contracting/compliance perspective: 

Call highlights (brief)
- Use case: customer financial data enrichment for EU customers; some PII is sent for tokenization and enrichment.
- Data residency: primary processing in EU region; potential occasional replication to US for analytics.
- Primary ask from FinWise: confirm our GDPR role, surface SOC 2 status, and provide DPA/SCC options.

Three near-term asks
1) Can you confirm whether FinWise will be data controller for this engagement? (From the call I understood yes, but want to record it.)
2) If you have an existing DPA template or specific clauses, please send them over (I can share our draft DPA as well).
3) Would you like us to complete your vendor security questionnaire (we can do OneTrust or a PDF questionnaire)? If so, please point me at the questionnaire or attach it.

Next steps from Redwood
- I will route the DPA request and SCC question to our legal team and propose a recommended SCC module and draft DPA.
- Lauren (cc’d) will take the lead on the security questionnaire and SOC 2 evidence.

If you can send the DPA template and an initial copy of the vendor questionnaire, we’ll prioritize this and aim to return a draft within 48 business hours.

Thanks,

Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-1289
Redwood Inference — Inference made predictable

P.S. Attaching the short call notes we captured to save time (no sensitive content).

From: Elena Koval <elena.koval@finwise.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: privacy@finwise.com
Date: 2027-04-21T11:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: FinWise privacy follow-up — DPA intake & SCC routing (post-demo)

Monica — thanks for the recap and the quick turnaround. Confirming: FinWise will be the data controller for the customer data flows described.

Attached is our standard DPA request PDF (FinWise_DPA_Request_20270421.pdf) — it includes the clauses our legal team prefers and a short questionnaire about subprocessors and data exports. A couple of specifics from our side:
- SOC 2: we require our vendors to have SOC 2 Type II or an explicit remediation plan with milestones (we can accept a SOC 2 in progress if there is a firm timeline).
- SCCs: we typically ask vendors to accept Processor Module SCCs for our vendors handling personal data (we can discuss module choice in more detail).
- Data transfers: any cross-border transfers need to be listed and we prefer when vendors support an SCC module that covers both controller-to-processor and processor-to-processor flows where applicable.

We also have a security questionnaire (OneTrust) — I can invite your security contact if you prefer. For now, please confirm who on your side will own the questionnaire and who legal should expect to coordinate with for the DPA redline.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Koval
Head of Privacy & Compliance | FinWise
elena.koval@finwise.com

Attachment: FinWise_DPA_Request_20270421.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-22T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: FinWise privacy follow-up — DPA intake & SCC routing (post-demo)

David — forwarding FinWise’s DPA request and the call notes. Key points for legal review: FinWise says they are controller; they prefer Processor Module SCCs; SOC 2 Type II required or remediation plan.

Attached: SCC_Options_Table.xlsx — internal comparison I prepared showing pros/cons of Modules (Processor vs Controller modules, combined flows). Lauren will take the questionnaire but I want legal to propose the DPA approach and preferred SCC module. Can you: 
- Confirm Redwood’s recommended position for controller/processor mapping and which SCC module we should accept/offer?
- Provide a near-term DPA draft we can send back (redline-ready) and an ask list for FinWise (e.g., subprocessors list, export controls, encryption at rest).

Elena — looping David (Redwood Legal) and Lauren (Customer Success) to coordinate next steps.

Thanks,
Monica

Attachment: SCC_Options_Table.xlsx

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, Elena Koval <elena.koval@finwise.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinWise privacy follow-up — DPA intake & SCC routing (post-demo)

Thanks for the context and the attachment(s). Quick guidance and proposed next steps below.

High-level mapping
- Role: Based on Monica’s summary and Elena’s confirmation, FinWise is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor for the described flows. We will document this clearly in the DPA.

SCC module recommendation
- Recommendation: Offer the EU Standard Contractual Clauses using the Processor-focused variant (commonly referenced as the SCC "Processor Module"). Rationale: FinWise is controller, Redwood acts as processor; the Processor Module provides the most straightforward mapping and is widely accepted by corporate legal teams.
- Note: If FinWise requires additional controller-to-controller flows (e.g., downstream sharing where FinWise is not the sole controller), we should be prepared to propose a combined/module approach — will confirm after questionnaire review.

SOC 2 handling
- Request: Ask FinWise if they will accept Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report (we have an up-to-date report from 2026) or whether they need a remediation plan and timeline. Lauren, please prepare the SOC 2 cover sheet and our current evidence bundle.

Immediate deliverables
1) I’ve prepared a short draft DPA (RW_DPA_draft_20270423.docx) reflecting Processor role and Processor Module SCCs — see attached for internal review.
2) Monica/Lauren: please ask FinWise to share the completed vendor questionnaire or invite our security contact to OneTrust. We can complete most sections quickly, but subcontractor details may take longer to reconcile.
3) Proposed timeline: return draft DPA within 48 business hours from now; aim to have SCC selection confirmed within one week after questionnaire completion.

Ask for FinWise (to include in reply)
- Confirm any required local SCC flavor (if their legal requires a specific annex).
- Provide any mandatory security controls beyond SOC 2 (e.g., specific encryption key management requirements, on-prem processing carve-outs).
- Share expected procurement timeline so we can align resource availability.

I’ll be available to join a short three-way call with FinWise legal if they prefer to walk through the DPA and SCC selection live.

David Kim
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: RW_DPA_draft_20270423.docx
